dedupe_keys.name: rapid collaborative research the effects of the 2017 central mexico earthquake on reinforced concrete buildings

description: RAPID/Collaborative Research: The Effects of the 2017 Central Mexico Earthquake on Reinforced Concrete Buildings is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Andreas Stavridis, University at Buffalo (buffalo.edu). This project contains the ambient vibration data of eleven buildings located in Mexico City obtained during a reconnaissance trip 5 months after the 2017 earthquake. The reconnaissance team included researchers from the University at Buffalo, University of Nebraska-Lincoln, UC San Diego, Cal Poly, San Luis Obispo, and was led by Purdue University. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-r8m0-qa07. Keywords: Mexico City, Ambient vibration data, damaged buildings. Published 2019-07-05. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
